clue.text: But it should have substantial beams

definitions.text: But it should have substantial beams

parts.words: But it should have substantial beams
parts.note: a house that is 'light' sounds as if it should not have heavy timbers, yet this coastal tower must send out strong beams of light

explanation.surface: A grumble about a building whose roof timbers ought to be sturdier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beams' reads as roof timbers, and a 'light' house sounds flimsy; the beams are rays from a lamp warning ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal tower's whole purpose is to shine powerful rays out to sea.

clue.text: Put down face upwards

indicators.note: upwards in a down clue means the word for face reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock

explanation.surface: Set something down with its front facing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upwards' turns DIAL round in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past tense of lay, to place something down.

clue.text: A GP's about to create openings

indicators.note: about means the letters of the doctor phrase are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor is ready to open some new surgeries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges A GPS (GP is a family doctor).
explanation.definitionFit: Gaps are openings or breaks in something.

clue.text: It certainly was a crisis for Lot's wife

definitions.text: It certainly was a crisis for Lot's wife

parts.words: It certainly was a crisis for Lot's wife
parts.note: in Genesis Lot's wife looked back and was changed into a pillar of salt, literally a moment of turning into a pillar

explanation.surface: A Bible story's moment of disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Lot's wife turned to look back at Sodom and became a pillar of salt: she turned, and became a point (pillar).
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive crisis is a moment where events change direction for good.

clue.text: Measure associated with Betty Martin

explanation.surface: A unit linked to a woman's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All my eye and Betty Martin' is an old phrase for nonsense, so Betty Martin goes with the eye; an optic is also a pub spirit measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's spirit dispenser gives a fixed measure, and to do with the eye matches the Betty Martin phrase.

clue.text: Age of Sweetness

parts.note: the phrase 'sweet' plus a teenage number is a stock description of youthful charm

explanation.surface: A period of history defined by sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet seventeen' is the stock phrase for girlish youth, so this is the age linked to sweetness.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock phrase pairs 'sweet' with this teenage age.

clue.text: Suitable meeting place for strikers ?

parts.note: strikers suggests workers on strike holding a meeting, but a stick for hitting a ball is a striker too, and a society's premises share that name

explanation.surface: Somewhere for workers on strike to gather.
explanation.walkthrough: The word names both a social society with its own premises and a golf stick or cudgel used for striking.
explanation.definitionFit: A society's clubhouse is a meeting place, and a golf stick or cudgel is a striking tool, so the word fits both.

clue.text: Features of the man in steel, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the phrase man in steel could be differently arranged

explanation.surface: Describing the face of a knight in armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges MAN IN STEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineaments are the distinctive lines of a face, its features.

clue.text: Bird on eastern ship shows gall

parts.note: a bittern is a wading bird of the heron family
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A heron on a ship from the east shows nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets the bird above the rest in this down light; 'gall' means rancour here, not cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Gall is a resentful sourness or rancour.

clue.text: The mood of a dictatorial grammarian

definitions.text: The mood of a dictatorial grammarian

parts.words: The mood of a dictatorial grammarian
parts.note: mood is a grammatical term for verb forms, and the one used for commands suits a bossy grammarian

explanation.surface: Describing the temper of a bossy language teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mood' looks like a temper, but in grammar it is a verb form; the form for giving orders suits a dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb form for commands ('Sit down!') is the grammatical mood of ordering, as a dictator would.

clue.text: Smack back — get fly

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for a smack from right to left

parts.note: a smack is a flavour or tang

explanation.surface: Swat the insect: hit it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TANG round.
explanation.definitionFit: A small biting insect is a kind of fly.

clue.text: The sharpness of some musicians

parts.note: sharpness suggests wit, but it means the raised tuning standard an orchestra plays to

explanation.surface: How clever some performers are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sharpness' reads as wit, but in music sharp means slightly high; this tuning standard is a little higher than normal.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestral tuning set slightly above standard is literally sharper in pitch.

clue.text: Unhappy at setting up a last-minute record ?

definitions.text: Unhappy at setting up a last-minute record ?

parts.words: Unhappy at setting up a last-minute record ?
parts.note: split as '...', a record put on the turntable at the last minute, while the word as a whole means unhappy

explanation.surface: Someone upset at having to put a record on so late.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it DISC ON SO LATE: a record (disc) put on at the last minute.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beyond comfort is deeply unhappy.

clue.text: Temperature at which I Ac comes into operation?

definitions.text: Temperature at which I Ac comes into operation?

parts.words: Temperature at which I Ac comes into operation?
parts.note: the temperature at which vapour ignites; I Ac, a short burst of current, would come on in a spark

explanation.surface: The heat at which a device switches on.
explanation.walkthrough: The term means the temperature at which a vapour ignites; the clue's 'I Ac' points to a flash of electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest temperature at which vapour from a liquid ignites is a technical temperature.

clue.text: Could a blonde be accused of this ?

definitions.text: Could a blonde be accused of this ?

parts.words: Could a blonde be accused of this ?
parts.note: a blonde is fair-haired, so she cannot be charged with lacking fairness, i.e. injustice

explanation.surface: Is it possible to blame a pale-haired woman for something?
explanation.walkthrough: A blonde is fair, so she could hardly be accused of being un-fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Injustice is lacking fairness, which a fair-haired person cannot be said to lack.

clue.text: Noble terrestrial resting-place

parts.note: terrestrial means of the land as opposed to sea
a resting-place for the dead is a grave

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's earthly tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: A landgrave was a German count holding a territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A landgrave was a German count with territorial rule, a title of nobility.

clue.text: "But yet I'l make double sure" (Macbeth)

parts.note: the quotation from Macbeth has a word missing between make and double, and that missing word is the answer

explanation.surface: A line spoken by Macbeth.
explanation.walkthrough: The full line is 'But yet I'll make assurance double sure': the clue prints it with the word cut out.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Macbeth's line means certainty or a guarantee.

clue.text: How a criminal comes when he's all washed up?

definitions.text: How a criminal comes when he's all washed up?

parts.words: How a criminal comes when he's all washed up?
parts.note: a crook who confesses is said to 'come' this way, and someone freshly washed is spotless

explanation.surface: A villain whose career is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washed up' looks like finished, but read as freshly washed it gives spotless; a criminal who confesses 'comes' that way.
explanation.definitionFit: To come out spotless, owning up honestly, is the idiom for a criminal's confession.

clue.text: One of the army's overheads was a staff officer eating endless fish

indicators.note: eating means the officer's letters take the fish inside them

parts.note: SO is the abbreviation for staff officer

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the fish is dropped

parts.note: hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: An army officer tucks into fish: an army expense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts HAKE to HAK, and 'eating' puts it inside SO. 'Overheads' looks like costs but means things worn on the head: a shako is a tall military cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall peaked military hat, something soldiers wear on their heads.

clue.text: An odd assertion made by girls abroad

indicators.note: odd means the letters of the following word are made strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: Some young women make a strange claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges ASSERTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Young unmarried Spanish women are addressed by this title, so these are girls in a foreign land.

clue.text: Not necessarily associations of craftsmen

parts.note: business alliances need not involve any artisans

explanation.surface: Unions that do not have to be guilds of artisans.
explanation.walkthrough: Craft can mean boats: split PARTNER SHIPS, it is paired craft, though business associations need involve no craftsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Business associations between partners are joint ventures of this kind.

clue.text: Jumping on board, that's the game

definitions.text: Jumping on board, that's the game

parts.words: Jumping on board, that's the game
parts.note: jumping on board suggests boarding a vehicle, but describes counters hopping over each other on a board

explanation.surface: Leaping aboard is the sport.
explanation.walkthrough: In this board game, pieces jump over others, as in Chinese chequers.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game where pieces jump across the board is this one.

clue.text: Press makes the bourgeoisie content

indicators.note: content, the inside of the word, means the letters are found within the bourgeoisie

explanation.surface: Newspapers please the middle class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like satisfied but means contents: the letters inside BOURGEOISIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone is to urge them strongly.

clue.text: Unnatural dwelling?

annotationWithheld.why: Unnatural dwelling? (4) as printed gives FLAT (unnatural note = flat; a flat is a dwelling), not PLAT as filed; no parse gives PLAT

clue.text: Generous fellow loses his head in Bucks

indicators.note: loses his head means the first letter of the word for a generous fellow goes

parts.note: a generous fellow is a giver

explanation.surface: A kind man is beheaded in Buckinghamshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is short for Buckinghamshire, an English county west of London; Iver is a village there.
explanation.definitionFit: Iver is a village in the county of Buckinghamshire, which is abbreviated Bucks.

clue.text: Cricket captain shows independence, making this declaration

definitions.text: Cricket captain shows independence, making this declaration

parts.words: Cricket captain shows independence, making this declaration
parts.note: a cricket captain 'declares' an innings closed, and a one-sided declaration of independence (Rhodesia's UDI) is this kind

explanation.surface: A cricket captain acts alone in calling an innings closed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the captain may declare, ending his side's innings. Rhodesia's 1965 UDI was a one-sided Declaration of Independence.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-sided declaration, made by one party alone, as in Rhodesia's UDI.

clue.text: The job that idle Jack should be taken to

definitions.text: The job that idle Jack should be taken to

parts.words: The job that idle Jack should be taken to
parts.note: to be taken to this is to be scolded, and the same word means a piece of work, fit for a lazy fellow

explanation.surface: Lazy Jack should be marched off to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken to' plus the word is the idiom for being scolded, and the word itself means a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A job or duty is a piece of work; being 'taken to' it is being reprimanded.

clue.text: Military force with an appearance of aloofness

explanation.surface: Troops who look standoffish.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit sent off from the main army is a military force; standing apart emotionally is aloofness.
